# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a workflow run
    # that queued BEHIND the concurrency group for the whole leg duration
    # (live: gh-317/gh-318 twins, 20:01→20:03); the in-run dedupe gate cannot
    # act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole run pending before any
    # job (incl. dedupe) starts. The awf guard skips status echoes at
    # evaluation, so no double EXECUTION — but the queue clutter was real.
    # Leg dispatching is dispatch-only: the SM dispatches review/rework
    # (workflow_dispatch, inputs.leg), the manual rework override (#544) is a
    # dispatch with leg=rework instead of the agent:rework label.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  factory:
    needs: dedupe
    if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'
    # TWO PINS, never conflated (see test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart):
    #   uses:  — the FACTORY HOME pin (dmtools-agentic-workflows). Moves
    #            only when the factory home changes; never bumped with
    #            the agents submodule.
    #   factory_ref: — the ENGINE pin (dmtools-agents, == the `agents`
    #            submodule gitlink). Bumps in lockstep with the submodule.
    # A branch ref would execute an unreviewed branch head at run start —
    # keep both immutable SHAs.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: d22a4f1032e2cd441200ed1a8309234985385fd2
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
# DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY (pack registry base) is read by the factory from
# this repo's VARIABLE of the same name — see dmtools-agents#574.

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      # gh-315: the sharded agents suite merges in `agents-gate` (the
      # matrix shards themselves are not required contexts, same as `test`).
      validation-checks: '["agents-gate","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-gate/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Frozen machine loop (same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: agents
    # resolve from dmtools-agents RELEASES by vars.AGENTS_VERSION).
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

# Merge Trigger — thin stub over the canonical pr_approved merge bot.
# All logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-merge-trigger.yml; the event triggers stay repo-side
# (workflow_run on Quality + issues:labeled re-entry — the label event
# must not be swallowed when CI hasn't run yet).
name: Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : CI passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']
    types: [completed]
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge-trigger.yml@main
    with:
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      remove_pr_label: true
      map_pr_labels: true
      gh_branch_pattern: true
    # `secrets: inherit` is safe here — unlike the other stubs, the AW
    # factory-merge-trigger declares NO `secrets:` block under
    # workflow_call, so required-secret validation cannot fail at startup;
    # its header prescribes inherit as the way to forward the optional
    # PAT (it reads secrets.PAT_TOKEN || github.token; explicitly mapping
    # an undeclared secret is rejected at call time).
    secrets: inherit

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 342
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/342
- **Title**: chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19 (kicker real ticks + per-SHA concurrency)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `pin/awf-kicker-fd84ab19` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +41
- **Deletions**: -44
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:00:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T08:17:14Z

## PR Description

Mechanical re-pin of the factory-workflow immutable SHA `e611e5f4` → `fd84ab19`. Brings two awf fixes:

- **awf #13** — kicker dispatches REAL ticks: a bare `gh workflow run` lands dryRun=true; the kicker now passes `-F dryRun=false`.
- **awf #14** — per-head-SHA concurrency: queued kickers are no longer superseded by every push (a pending run in a shared group is ALWAYS displaced — `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING one). Required contexts (`sm-liveness`/`head-completeness`) stop dying CANCELLED on fresh heads. Root cause of dmtools-agents #682 (live: fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03; eight branches cancelled in one 36s dev-wave 06:21–06:22 2026-10-04).

Refs: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#13, #14 · IstiN/dmtools-agents#682 (+ standing remedy in dmtools-agents#695).

Note: if your kicker stub declares its OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too — a caller-level global group re-introduces the supersession locally (dmtools-agents scoped its stub in #695; fa/dart stubs declare none).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file carries
# only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository event
# triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a workflow run
    # that queued BEHIND the concurrency group for the whole leg duration
    # (live: gh-317/gh-318 twins, 20:01→20:03); the in-run dedupe gate cannot
    # act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole run pending before any
    # job (incl. dedupe) starts. The awf guard skips status echoes at
    # evaluation, so no double EXECUTION — but the queue clutter was real.
    # Leg dispatching is dispatch-only: the SM dispatches review/rework
    # (workflow_dispatch, inputs.leg), the manual rework override (#544) is a
    # dispatch with leg=rework instead of the agent:rework label.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  factory:
    needs: dedupe
    if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'
    # TWO PINS, never conflated (see test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart):
    #   uses:  — the FACTORY HOME pin (dmtools-agentic-workflows). Moves
    #            only when the factory home changes; never bumped with
    #            the agents submodule.
    #   factory_ref: — the ENGINE pin (dmtools-agents, == the `agents`
    #            submodule gitlink). Bumps in lockstep with the submodule.
    # A branch ref would execute an unreviewed branch head at run start —
    # keep both immutable SHAs.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: d22a4f1032e2cd441200ed1a8309234985385fd2
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
# DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY (pack registry base) is read by the factory from
# this repo's VARIABLE of the same name — see dmtools-agents#574.

- `factory_ref` remains an immutable SHA (d22a4f10...) — good, engine pin intact.

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      # gh-315: the sharded agents suite merges in `agents-gate` (the
      # matrix shards themselves are not required contexts, same as `test`).
      validation-checks: '["agents-gate","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-gate/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:

    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

  pull-requests: write

jobs:

    if: >-

name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 342
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/342
- **Title**: chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19 (kicker real ticks + per-SHA concurrency)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `pin/awf-kicker-fd84ab19` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +41
- **Deletions**: -44
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:00:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T08:17:14Z

## PR Description

Mechanical re-pin of the factory-workflow immutable SHA `e611e5f4` → `fd84ab19`. Brings two awf fixes:

- **awf #13** — kicker dispatches REAL ticks: a bare `gh workflow run` lands dryRun=true; the kicker now passes `-F dryRun=false`.
- **awf #14** — per-head-SHA concurrency: queued kickers are no longer superseded by every push (a pending run in a shared group is ALWAYS displaced — `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING one). Required contexts (`sm-liveness`/`head-completeness`) stop dying CANCELLED on fresh heads. Root cause of dmtools-agents #682 (live: fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03; eight branches cancelled in one 36s dev-wave 06:21–06:22 2026-10-04).

Refs: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#13, #14 · IstiN/dmtools-agents#682 (+ standing remedy in dmtools-agents#695).

Note: if your kicker stub declares its OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too — a caller-level global group re-introduces the supersession locally (dmtools-agents scoped its stub in #695; fa/dart stubs declare none).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file carries
# only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository event
# triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a workflow run
    # that queued BEHIND the concurrency group for the whole leg duration
    # (live: gh-317/gh-318 twins, 20:01→20:03); the in-run dedupe gate cannot
    # act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole run pending before any
    # job (incl. dedupe) starts. The awf guard skips status echoes at
    # evaluation, so no double EXECUTION — but the queue clutter was real.
    # Leg dispatching is dispatch-only: the SM dispatches review/rework
    # (workflow_dispatch, inputs.leg), the manual rework override (#544) is a
    # dispatch with leg=rework instead of the agent:rework label.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  factory:
    needs: dedupe
    if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'
    # TWO PINS, never conflated (see test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart):
    #   uses:  — the FACTORY HOME pin (dmtools-agentic-workflows). Moves
    #            only when the factory home changes; never bumped with
    #            the agents submodule.
    #   factory_ref: — the ENGINE pin (dmtools-agents, == the `agents`
    #            submodule gitlink). Bumps in lockstep with the submodule.
    # A branch ref would execute an unreviewed branch head at run start —
    # keep both immutable SHAs.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: d22a4f1032e2cd441200ed1a8309234985385fd2
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
# DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY (pack registry base) is read by the factory from
# this repo's VARIABLE of the same name — see dmtools-agents#574.

- The comment block above `uses:` still says "A branch ref would execute an unreviewed branch head at run start — keep both immutable SHAs." — now directly contradicted by `@main` on the very next line.
- `factory_ref` remains an immutable SHA (d22a4f10...) — good, engine pin intact.

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      # gh-315: the sharded agents suite merges in `agents-gate` (the
      # matrix shards themselves are not required contexts, same as `test`).
      validation-checks: '["agents-gate","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-gate/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 342
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/342
- **Title**: chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19 (kicker real ticks + per-SHA concurrency)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `pin/awf-kicker-fd84ab19` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +41
- **Deletions**: -44
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:00:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T08:17:14Z

## PR Description

Mechanical re-pin of the factory-workflow immutable SHA `e611e5f4` → `fd84ab19`. Brings two awf fixes:

- **awf #13** — kicker dispatches REAL ticks: a bare `gh workflow run` lands dryRun=true; the kicker now passes `-F dryRun=false`.
- **awf #14** — per-head-SHA concurrency: queued kickers are no longer superseded by every push (a pending run in a shared group is ALWAYS displaced — `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING one). Required contexts (`sm-liveness`/`head-completeness`) stop dying CANCELLED on fresh heads. Root cause of dmtools-agents #682 (live: fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03; eight branches cancelled in one 36s dev-wave 06:21–06:22 2026-10-04).

Refs: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#13, #14 · IstiN/dmtools-agents#682 (+ standing remedy in dmtools-agents#695).

Note: if your kicker stub declares its OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too — a caller-level global group re-introduces the supersession locally (dmtools-agents scoped its stub in #695; fa/dart stubs declare none).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.
